question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 26 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of auth v2.23 to ap-south likely caused the increase in p95 latency.
why_chain: The deployment of auth v2.23 to ap-south occurred 220 minutes before the change point.
The p95 latency increased from 137 ms to 298 ms, a significant increase.
The deployment of auth v2.23 is a known change that could affect latency.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in request volume may have contributed to the latency increase.
why_chain: The request volume increased from 1236 per 5 min to 5418 per 5 min, a significant increase.
The increase in request volume could have overwhelmed the system, leading to higher latency.
The deployment of auth v2.23 to ap-south is a known change that could affect request volume.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in error rate may be related to the deployment of auth v2.23.
why_chain: The error rate increased from 0.41% to 0.81%, a significant increase.
The deployment of auth v2.23 to ap-south is a known change that could affect error rates.
The increase in error rate could be a symptom of the deployment of auth v2.23.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency is due to a configuration change.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a config_change as the cause of the latency increase.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency is due to a dependency issue with an external service.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports a dependency issue as the cause of the latency increase.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency is due to an infrastructure issue.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence supports an infrastructure issue as the cause of the latency increase.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region ap-south rose from 137 ms to 298 ms (+117%), with a change point at 2026-03-26T06:10:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region ap-south: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for region ap-south rose (1236 per 5 min before, 5418 per 5 min after, +338%).
At the same time, error rate for region ap-south rose (0.41% before, 0.81% after, +97%).
Request volume 3x normal in ap-south (ap-south; 12 min after the change; record R012)
Deployed auth v2.23 to ap-south (routine release) (auth, ap-south; 220 min before the change; record R009)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (ap-south; 20 min after the change; record R013)
Deployed checkout v2.3 to eu-west (routine release) (checkout, eu-west; 74 min before the change; record R010)
auth: WARN slow query 1.2s on report endpoint (single occurrence) (auth, us-east; 63 min before the change; record R011)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 220 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✗ Request volume also rose, so a traffic explanation is still open.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records from the hour before the change

actions.action: Roll back the deployment of auth v2.23 to ap-south
Monitor request volume and error rates closely in ap-south
Review and optimize the autoscaler in ap-south
